title: Aseptic Technique in Practice

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

summary: Practical habits that minimize contamination risk to cultures and exposure risk to personnel during routine microbiological work.
explanation: Aseptic technique is a continuous discipline applied throughout a procedure — from decontaminating the bench before starting, to minimizing the time containers are open, to flaming/sterilizing tools between uses, to decontaminating the bench again at the end.
keyPractices: Disinfect the work surface before and after work.
Keep culture container lids/caps closed except during the brief moment of transfer.
Sterilize loops/needles before and after each use.
Work close to a flame or within validated laminar/biosafety airflow appropriate to the organism.
commonMistakes: Setting an open culture tube down on the bench between steps.
Reusing a loop without re-sterilizing it between different cultures.
